runs.content: Sunday's rotation focus is 'whichever domain has gone longest without a deep-dive.' Among the Friday-group domains (Lightfin, Games, Cooking, Sports Betting, Work), Lightfin was covered last Sunday (2026-09-06), so today's deep-read targeted Games — unchanged since the 2026-07-27 discovery that all four prototype stubs are real files, just filed under the wrong domain folders; games/overview.md and games/prototypes.md are still the exact same unpopulated placeholder tables from 2026-05-01, and raw/games/ has no new files. Nothing new surfaced there. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-12, Saturday full sweep), log.md otherwise shows only routine Finance-internal activity: an mf-update Magic Formula run and the first-ever run of the new strategy-feedback-loop task (added 2026-09-10) confirming its own Burry-aware entry-avoidance rule worked as designed (MU/QCOM/ASML/CAT drove the worst paper-trading losses in strategies B/C/D) — already correctly wired into finance/models/model-portfolio-management.md, not a gap. Two genuinely new, non-duplicate cross-domain connections cleared the bar instead, both from Saturday's podcast-summarizer batch that hadn't yet been checked against Finance: (1) Ed Zitron's newly-ingested 'AI is the world's greatest bubble' episode (podcast-diary-of-a-ceo-ed-zitron-episode, circular financing between hyperscalers and AI labs, dot-com parallels) makes almost the identical argument finance/models/model-hyperscaler-gpu-token-debt-2026-08-05.md already built a full off-balance-sheet debt map around — that model page explicitly cross-references Burry's own circular-financing thesis and the BIS Annual Economic Report, but nothing links it to Zitron's episode, which currently only cross-links within Podcasts. (2) Dividend Talk EP 305 ('Should Cyclical Stocks Be in Your Dividend Portfolio') names exactly the dividend-safety test missing from finance/ideas/ideas-dividend-undervalued.md, which already carries two cyclical names (AGCO, Lithia Motors) flagged internally as riskier picks but never tested against a cyclical-vs-compounder framework — its own 'What Makes a Dividend Sustainable' section only covers moat, capital allocation, and undervaluation. Checked the open sections for resolution: nothing showed clear signs of being actioned since 2026-09-12.

Saturday is the full-sweep day — skim every domain's overview/index page rather than deep-reading one, bias toward cross-domain connections over investigation ideas. Since the last thinker run (2026-09-11, a quiet Friday), log.md shows a Finance clippings-sorter run (5 new Morningstar pieces, 10 new watchlist stocks: ASML, Synopsys, CRH, Magna, ResMed, Warner Music Group, Amcor, Brown-Forman, Hormel, Kimberly-Clark) and six new podcast-summarizer pages (CyberHack: The Conti Files, Odd Lots on bond yields, Dividend Talk EP305, Diary of a CEO x Ed Zitron, Prof G Markets on bond/inflation, Behind the Balance Sheet x Rich Pzena). Two genuinely new, non-duplicate cross-domain connections cleared the bar: (1) Two freshly-listened podcasts — Odd Lots and Prof G Markets, both on the recent Treasury-yield surge — land on exactly the same bond-market-stress story Finance's own Dalio Big Debt Cycle piece (source-dalio-bond-market-supply-demand-2026-08-28, 9 red-flag indicators) and the Bessent-stablecoin piece have been tracking since late August; the two podcasts already cross-link each other but neither links to either Finance source, and vice versa. (2) Rich Pzena's podcast recounts his firm underperforming the S&P by 60 percentage points during the 2000 dot-com bubble before a turnaround — a real, quantified historical precedent for the identical mania Michael Burry explicitly names as his own analogue (source-burry-trading-post-2026-06-12: 'a repeat of his 2000 playbook... while the market chased a different mania (dot-coms then; AI infrastructure now)') — relevant right now given Burry's own LULU position is currently in the underperform-and-hold phase Pzena's story shows resolving well. Neither page cites the other. A third candidate (ResMed's fresh watchlist entry — the market leader in sleep-apnea/CPAP devices — versus Health's own Nestor 'Breath' research on mouth-breathing/poor-sleep mechanisms) was considered but set aside as the weaker, more inferential of the three; the wiki's own ResMed entry only says 'digital-health M&A,' not sleep apnea specifically. No investigation idea cleared the bar today — nothing in the new Morningstar batch or podcast additions pointed at a concrete, actionable gap beyond what's already open. Checked the open sections for resolution: nothing showed clear signs of being actioned since 2026-09-11.
